general_information.Description: The course is an intermediate-level course in macroeconomics, including topics in international, monetary, and financial economics. The goal of the course is to provide a coherent framework for analyzing macroeconomic events, such as business cycles (recessions and booms) and long-run growth, their impact on financial markets, and to discuss macroeconomic policy. In all parts of the course, theories will be applied to current economic events. Particular emphasis will be placed on the relation between macroeconomic events and financial markets. Finishing this course, students will be well-versed in macroeconomic and finance areas, be able to realize the implications of real-life macroeconomic policy/ events on the global financial markets.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 2. Actively participate in class activities 3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 5. Read the textbook in advance 6. Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify the Structure and measurement of the national economy
Describe the Consumption, Saving, Investment in the Open Economy
Explain how the economy and works in the long-run and short run
Understand, analyze and evaluate Monetary Policy and Government Budget
Perform independent and collaborative analyis on the Macroeconomy

assessments.Question Type: Each student should make at least 1 individual presentation during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook. In addition, students are required to do exercises and other activities
assessments.Note: Participation scores will be given based on students' class attendance, preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussions, and building upon others’ comments. Class participation accounts for 15% of the final score.

assessments.Question Type: Exercises/essay questions: 3 short questions which can be divided into further sub-parts covering important issues
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: For the essay section, there are 1 question on one or more of the chapters 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 2 questions on two or more of the chapters 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15.

assessments.Duration: Presentation in class (end of the course)
assessments.Question Type: Suggestion: Choose some case study using the studied models to evaluate and explain the situation.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Thinking creatively, making decisions, solving problems, Personal qualities: Individual responsibility, self-esteem, sociability, self-management, and integrity.
assessments.Note: Member scores need not be the same within each group. Recommended 30% for presentation, 70% for report.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Integration of acquired knowledge and skills. Quiz 1 covers chapters 1, 2, 4. Quiz 2 covers chapters 8, 9, 12.

Multiple choice For the multiple choice section, estimated 20% of the materials before the midterm (Chapters: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7), and 80% of the materials after the midterm (Chapters: 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15).
